findings.evidenceJa: 箸休めになんか作っとこう
findings.governingReading: Shirou intends a light 箸休め, which makes accidentally producing a second main course specifically absurd.
findings.explanation: A palate-resting small dish becomes simply another dish.

findings.evidenceJa: 鶏肉を観音開きに切って
findings.governingReading: Shirou opens the tender along both sides to make a broad sheet for flattening and wrapping vegetables.
findings.explanation: Butterflying the chicken becomes filleting it.

findings.highlight: the saury fish that's supposed to be the main dish is still waiting to be broiled
findings.evidenceJa: メインにはとっくに秋刀魚さまが鎮座ましましている
findings.governingReading: Shirou's mock-courtly personification elevates the existing main dish and sets up the two-suns rhetoric.
findings.explanation: The saury already enthroned as ‘Lord Saury’ becomes a fish merely waiting to be broiled.

findings.evidenceJa: 六時半をちょっと過ぎたころ
findings.governingReading: Taiga arrives a little beyond the half hour, thirty minutes after Sakura.
findings.explanation: A time slightly after six-thirty becomes exactly half past six.

findings.highlight: I made you do so much yesterday
findings.governingReading: Because he was the recipient of her care or assistance, he intended to repay it by letting her rest this morning.
findings.explanation: Sakura having helped Shirou yesterday becomes Shirou having made her do work.

findings.highlight: making bento so early in the morning
findings.evidenceJa: 朝五時に起きて弁当を作る
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks getting up at five to make a bento must be hard even for someone who enjoys cooking.
findings.explanation: Getting up at five becomes cooking 'so early.' The specific cost to Sakura's sleep is less concrete, while Shirou's concern remains.

findings.highlight: you shared your bento with me
findings.evidenceJa: お弁当のおかずだって、先輩に分けてもらいました
findings.governingReading: Sakura cites the division of Shirou's prepared side dishes while she herself cooks the additional rice.
findings.explanation: Shirou sharing bento side dishes becomes sharing his bento as a whole.

findings.highlight: she still never listens to a word I say
findings.evidenceJa: 何を言ってもこんな風に返されてしまう
findings.governingReading: Her polite, reasoned replies repeatedly meet his objections; the narration does not say she ignores him.
findings.explanation: Sakura answering whatever concern Shirou raises in this fashion becomes never listening to a word he says.

findings.highlight: taking care of Fuji-nee and me is just a burden
findings.evidenceJa: 俺や藤ねえの世話にかまけてたら大変だぞ
findings.governingReading: He values her help but fears it will crowd out her own life and chosen pleasures.
findings.explanation: Shirou warning that preoccupation with caring for him and Taiga will be hard on Sakura becomes declaring the care itself ‘just a burden.’

findings.highlight: I feel like I'm getting there.
findings.evidenceJa: もうすぐ射程距離だったりします
findings.governingReading: Sakura playfully says Shirou's cooking is nearly within range, linking her cooking ambition to the archery hobby just mentioned.
findings.explanation: “Getting there” loses Sakura's archery joke about bringing Shirou within range. Her ambition to surpass him and her confident challenge remain.

findings.highlight: there's no denying that she's almost better than me in the kitchen
findings.evidenceJa: 紛れもない事実で狙われているのか俺
findings.governingReading: His concession that her ability is genuinely close continues the firing-range joke by casting himself as the quarry.
findings.explanation: Shirou asking whether he is literally being targeted disappears into a plain kitchen-skill comparison.

findings.evidenceJa: そんなの目の仇にしますっ
findings.governingReading: She accepts his ‘why make me the enemy?’ framing and forcefully insists that his food being tastier is unacceptable.
findings.explanation: Sakura emphatically making Shirou's superior cooking her target becomes merely setting a high bar.

findings.highlight: I stick my chopsticks in the fish's nicely colored belly
findings.evidenceJa: 焼けた腹に箸をあてて
findings.governingReading: Shirou applies the chopsticks to the browned belly and checks the cook, without stating that he pierces it.
findings.explanation: Touching the fish's belly with chopsticks to test doneness becomes sticking the chopsticks into it.

findings.evidenceJa: その手の痣、なんですか
findings.governingReading: Her gaze fixes on the mark before Shirou himself consciously notices it.
findings.explanation: Sakura asking specifically what the bruise on Shirou's hand is becomes asking generally what happened to his hand.

findings.highlight: Sakura looks ill, and she's fallen silent.
findings.evidenceJa: 気分が優れないのか、桜は押し黙っている
findings.governingReading: Her silence prompts a tentative explanation from his limited viewpoint.
findings.explanation: Shirou wondering whether Sakura feels unwell becomes the observation that she looks ill.

findings.highlight: I'm going to find something to cover this.
findings.evidenceJa: 湿布か何か貼ってくる
findings.governingReading: Shirou intends a basic therapeutic measure, not merely concealment or bandaging.
findings.explanation: Applying a compress or similar treatment becomes finding something to cover the mark.

findings.highlight: Sakura being so awkward and distraught
findings.evidenceJa: 気まずそうに俯いていた桜
findings.governingReading: Shirou is troubled by her downcast, uncomfortable posture but does not identify a more intense emotional state.
findings.explanation: Sakura looking down awkwardly becomes being both awkward and distraught.

findings.highlight: she hardly took a bite of her breakfast
findings.evidenceJa: 朝食は一口も喉を通らず
findings.governingReading: She eats none of the breakfast; this zero quantity is the fact Shirou uses against her claim of energy.
findings.explanation: Not a single bite passing Sakura's throat becomes her hardly taking a bite.
